title: Emmanuel Rodriguez emotional after Twins call-up: ‘Full disclosure: I cried’
content:
MINNEAPOLIS — Whether it was his ill-timed thumb injury in May plus a lengthy rehab, or seeing his other talented young teammates get the nod, Emmanuel Rodriguez patiently waited his turn.

But at long last, the Minnesota Twins prospect’s phone rang with life-changing news of a promotion to the big leagues. The Twins announced on Saturday they were calling up Rodriguez, whom The Athletic’s Keith Law rated as baseball’s No. 34 prospect in May.

Rodriguez, 23, received an emotional phone call from Triple-A manager Brian Dinkelman on Friday night and then shared the news with his family.

“Full disclosure: I cried,” Rodriguez said through an interpreter. “Everything happens at the right time. Earlier in the year, before the injury, I knew it was going to be my time, my moment. Things happen, but everything works out the way it’s supposed to work out.”

With the way their season is going, the Twins figured, why not give Rodriguez, who originally signed with the Twins for $2.5 million in 2019, a look now? The team fell again on Friday night, a 5-2 loss to the Cleveland Guardians that dropped them 5 1/2 games back in the race for the final American League wild-card spot with 15 to play. Since Aug. 1, the Twins are just 13-23.

Rodriguez — who won’t have any major-league options left next season despite never reaching the big leagues — returned to minor-league action on July 28, having missed nearly three months after suffering a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his left thumb on May 1.

He’s played 33 games since, hitting .289/.427/.479 with five home runs and 18 RBIs in 150 plate appearances.

With Byron Buxton out for the season and Walker Jenkins and Trevor Larnach struggling to hit, the Twins elected to see what Rodriguez can offer.

“It is important, because he is out of options next year,” Twins manager Derek Shelton said. “We do think he’s part of our future. But getting him major-league at-bats in the last (15) games, we thought was very beneficial.”

At the time he suffered his thumb injury, Rodriguez was squarely on the team’s radar. James Outman and Matt Wallner both started the season in a slump, and Rodriguez was off to a hot start, producing a .923 OPS in 25 games at Triple A. But then he slid headfirst into first base and tore his thumb.

“It was a real conversation,” general manager Jeremy Zoll said. “It was definitely a topic on our minds, all the different factors. Unfortunately, it didn’t go that way with the injury. Once he had to get through that whole rehab process, we wanted to make sure we got him a number of games to get his feet back under him and go from there.”

These days, Rodriguez, who’s been limited to 353 minor-league games because of injuries, is sliding feet first. At the team’s behest, he’s also been more aggressive at the plate, which has led to a 4 percent reduction in his strikeout rate and a slight increase in home runs.

Rodriguez is essentially a three-true-outcome player “with some real athleticism,” Zoll said. Though the Twins see Jenkins as the better candidate to handle center field, the expectation is Rodriguez can play there, and that’s where he will start his first game on Saturday.

After seeing Triple-A teammates Jenkins, Kaelen Culpepper and Gabby Gonzalez all get promoted in the past few months, Rodriguez is finally here.

“It’s just a full-circle moment, but they did their thing,” Rodriguez said. “They deserved their promotions, and I knew my chance was coming. Now I’ve put it all together, and we’re here ready to go.”
